rounds.text: Kross Ltd is materially undervalued by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of 21.8x and P/B of 2.58x, which sits below sector benchmarks of 25.2x and 2.86x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. The business is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 30% and an outstanding 5-year compounded profit growth of 63% [E14, E17]. Valuation analysis reveals a significant margin of safety at 46.6% with intrinsic value estimated at Rs 367 per share, while a reverse DCF shows the current price of Rs 196 only prices in a modest 9.4% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case assumption [E2, E39, E40, E41]. Furthermore, profitability metrics outperform the broader sector, with an ROCE of 15.29% against a sector benchmark of 14.4% and an ROA of 9.06% versus the sector's 7% [E8, E10]. Technical strength confirms this positive trajectory, as the stock trades comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with the 50-day crossing above the 200-day [E44], all supported by a favorable macro sector tailwind in Automobile & Auto Components [E63, E65]. Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional holdings have declined alongside negative money flow, and free cash flow stands at a negative Rs -72 Cr due to capital expenditure build-up [E30, E36, E37, E38].

While the broader company profile shows multi-year profit expansion, severe cracks are emerging in cash generation and institutional conviction [E17, E28, E36, E37]. Operating cash flow for Mar 2026 sits at just 51 percent of reported profit, dragging free cash flow down to a staggering negative Rs 72 Cr [E28, E30]. This cash disconnect is underscored by a ballooning in working capital days from 87.2 days to 125 days, alongside a spike in borrowings from Rs 34 Cr to Rs 54 Cr [E33, E55]. Smart money is actively fleeing the counter, evidenced by foreign institutions slashing holdings from 5.93 percent to 2.51 percent and domestic institutions cutting stakes from 9.54 percent to 6.05 percent [E36, E37]. Operational momentum is also visibly cooling, with quarterly and yearly operating margins locked in an inconsistent trend and earnings growth actively decelerating [E26, E27, E61]. Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 21.8x with a strong 5-year sales compounded growth rate of 30 percent and a high rules-based screen score [E1, E14, E56].

Conceded: operating cash flow sits at 51 percent of reported profit for Mar 2026, leading to a negative free cash flow of Rs 72 Cr alongside rising borrowings [E28, E30, E33], and institutional holdings have indeed declined [E36, E37]. However, this cash drain and capital tie-up directly coincide with a massive 1500 percent surge in Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) to Rs 16 Cr, indicating a deliberate and aggressive capex build-up phase rather than structural failure [E34]. Furthermore, the bear's narrative of fleeing smart money ignores the fact that promoters have actively increased their stake to 68.57 percent [E35], demonstrating internal conviction. The valuation does not reflect this growth posture, as a reverse DCF reveals that the current price assumes a mere 9.4 percent earnings growth against a historical 5-year profit CAGR of 63.5 percent [E17, E41, E53]. Technical momentum remains firmly positive with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E44], supported by an Automobile and Auto Components sector tailwind score of +0.53 [E63, E65].

Conceded: promoters have increased their stake to 68.57 percent [E35]. However, the bull characterizes the severe negative free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr and weak 0.51x cash conversion as a deliberate capex phase tied to a surge in Capital Work in Progress [E28, E30, E34], yet borrowings have simultaneously jumped from Rs 34 Cr to Rs 54 Cr while working capital days have blown out from 87.2 days to 125 days [E33, E55]. This divergence between reported profits and actual cash generation points to deep operational strains rather than benign growth investments. Furthermore, dismissing institutional outflows ignores persistent negative money flow alongside sharp declines in holdings from both foreign and domestic institutions [E36, E37, E38, E62]. The screen specifically flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E61], operating margins remain inconsistent [E26, E27], and the company pays a zero dividend yield [E4, E54]. Finally, leaning on historical profit growth to justify future expectations [E17, E41] is contradicted by explicit evidence that current earnings growth is slowing down [E61].
